result.title: Rethinking Unsupervised Cross-Modal Homography Estimation:Spatially Aware Representations and Geometric Consistency Learning
result.summary: Unsupervised cross-modal homography estimation is challenging because appearance differences obscure shared geometric structures. Separating modality transfer from homography estimation helps reduce these differences, but accurate alignment still requires effective geometric representations and consistency constraints on the two subtasks. We propose GeoCo (Geometry-Aware and Consistency-Constrained Homography Estimation), a framework that addresses these two requirements without cross-modal transformation labels. Its homography estimator, RVHomo, adapts hierarchical features from a frozen vision foundation model (VFM) and fuses them with local CNN features to capture structural context and spatial detail. Two geometric consistency constraints encourage modality transfer to preserve geometry and homography predictions to remain consistent under synthetic geometric transformations. Through two-stage progressive distillation, we further obtain GeoCo-D, which uses the lightweight RVHomo-D estimator. An intermediate model first learns to perform cross-modal matching without modality transfer, then transfers prediction and feature knowledge to the student, eliminating online VFM extraction. Experiments on GoogleMap, OPT-SAR, FSD, and VIS-IR show that GeoCo reduces mean average corner error by 17.4-46.7% relative to the best-performing baseline on each dataset. GeoCo-D also outperforms all compared baselines while using 98.5% fewer parameters and 70.4% fewer FLOPs than the complete GeoCo teacher.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GeoCo 框架做无监督跨模态单应估计：RVHomo 融合冻结视觉基础模型的分层特征与 CNN 局部特征以兼顾结构上下文与空间细节，并施加两项几何一致性约束，再用两阶段渐进蒸馏得到轻量学生模型 GeoCo-D。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“合成几何变换下预测须保持一致”的约束与分层特征融合可供核查，可能作为让内部 latent 状态保留任务必要几何信息、筛选视觉证据的训练监督线索，但论文本身不涉及 VLM 推理或 latent 状态生成。
